message.content:
Yes—noise complaints in Atlanta are handled by the City of Atlanta Police Department.  
Here’s how you can file one:

| Step | What to do | Contact |
|------|------------|---------|
| 1 | **Call** the Atlanta Police Department’s non‑emergency line at **404‑656‑4000**. | Phone |
| 2 | **Use the online portal**: visit the City of Atlanta’s official website and navigate to “Noise Complaints” under the “Public Safety” section. You’ll find a form you can fill out electronically. | https://www.atlantaga.gov/ |
| 3 | **Visit a local precinct** if you prefer in‑person. Precincts are located throughout the city; you can find the nearest one on the website. | In‑person |

**What information will be needed?**

- Your name and contact details (optional but helpful).
- The address or location of the noise source.
- A description of the noise (e.g., loud music, construction, barking dogs).
- Time(s) when the noise occurs.
- Any relevant evidence (photos, videos, audio recordings).

**When to file?**  
If the noise is occurring during a time when it is prohibited by local ordinances (typically 10 p.m.–7 a.m.), you can file a complaint immediately. For other times, you may still file a complaint if the noise is excessive or disruptive.

**Follow‑up:**  
After filing, the police will investigate and may issue a warning or citation if the noise violates city ordinances. If you’re not satisfied with the outcome, you can appeal through the City of Atlanta’s administrative process.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like more detailed instructions or links to specific ordinances!
